name: User-level publish rule and non-admin site workflow

pr.title: Add the publish rule to the user's Claude Code settings, and write the site workflow for a non-admin
pr.head: 9a4c1b68abe81af4cc49aeb09797b5e552e1d39b

summary: project init used to add the Claude Code allow rule Bash(project review publish *) to the repository's .claude/settings.json. In a repository that ignores .claude/, the rule lived only in the one checkout where someone ran init, so fresh clones and background worktrees had their clean self-review publishes refused as self-approval. Committing the file instead would make an auto-mode exemption team policy. This pull request moves the rule into the person's own settings: ~/.claude/settings.json, or settings.json in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

The gate does not change. init adds the rule only at a terminal or with --publish-rule, an agent run only reports it, and configuration can only turn it off. The file is written through a symlink, such as one into a dotfiles repository, and reported with the home directory shown as ~. A repository's own .claude/settings.json is never read or written.

The second change lets a non-admin's init write the site workflow beside the gh commands it prints for an admin, instead of asking for a second init run. A workflow merged before the admin acts fails at actions/configure-pages while no Pages site exists, and site build --check-visibility refuses a private repository's public site, so it cannot publish early.

groups.title: The publish rule moves to the user's settings
groups.kicker: permissions.py finds the user's Claude Code settings and writes the rule through any link
intro: allow_publish no longer takes the repository root. settings_path picks $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json when that variable is set, and $HOME/.claude/settings.json otherwise. shown reports the path with the home directory as ~. The base's guard that kept a file linking outside the repository is gone, because a user settings file linked into a dotfiles repository is the common case. write_through already swaps the new content in at the link's resolved target.

The tests move the settings fixture from the repository into a temporary HOME created outside the repository, and unset CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so the suite cannot reach real settings. New tests cover writing through a dotfiles link, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and leaving a repository's own settings file byte-for-byte unchanged.
concepts: User-level allow rules take effect without Claude Code's workspace trust dialog, so the terminal-or---publish-rule gate is now the only human checkpoint.
Report mode, which is how an agent's init runs, reads the user file and never writes it.

checks.text: Every test that can reach allow_publish runs under RepositoryTestCase.setUp, with HOME at a temporary directory and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset, or passes --no-publish-rule, as InitSiteTests.init does.
publish_rule is add only with --publish-rule or when stdin is a terminal. review.publish_rule = true without a terminal still only reports.

src/projector/permissions.py:84 (P2, open): write_through runs outside any OSError handler. A settings link whose target directory is not writable makes init print a bare Permission denied and exit 65, before it reports the files it wrote or sets up the site. Return kept with the error instead.
src/projector/permissions.py:80 (suggestion): in a repository whose own settings carry the rule, an agent's init now says auto mode refuses the clean review, which is not true there.

files.note: settings_path, shown, and allow_publish without the repository root; the write at line 84 has no OSError handler
setUp isolates HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; new link, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and repository-settings tests

groups.title: A non-admin gets the site workflow
groups.kicker: NeedsAdmin carries the workflow init wrote, and init reports it with the admin's commands
intro: When enable_pages raises NeedsAdmin, init_site appends the homepage command as before and now writes the workflow, attaching the result to the error as workflow before re-raising. run appends that file action to the files it reports, whether or not --site turns the skip into an InitError. NeedsAdmin.steps no longer tells the user to run init again.

Every other refusal still raises a plain SpecError before a workflow is written: a branch site or another deployer without --site, a missing gh, and an admin whose private site GitHub will not make private.
concepts: A workflow on the default branch is harmless before Pages exists: configure-pages fails without a site, and --check-visibility refuses a private repository's public site.

checks.text: error.workflow is set only in the NeedsAdmin handler of init_site, and NeedsAdmin.__init__ defaults it to None, so the isinstance check in run covers every raise.
With --site, the workflow is written and listed in InitError.files before init exits 65, which is what test_writes_the_workflow_for_a_non_admin_whether_or_not_the_site_is_set_up asserts.
The rerun after the admin's commands reports the workflow as unchanged and makes no GitHub writes.

files.note: init_site writes the workflow on NeedsAdmin; run reports it; allow_publish loses its root argument
NeedsAdmin gains workflow and a steps text without a second init
Non-admin runs now expect the workflow created, then unchanged on the rerun

groups.title: Docs and skills
groups.kicker: The CLI reference, site guide, README, and two skills follow both changes
intro: docs/cli.md rewrites the settings entry for the user file, adds how ~ and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR show in output, and replaces the non-admin example with one that writes the workflow, then says how to start the workflow once the admin is done. review-changes now asks a refused publisher's user to run project init at a terminal instead of committing .claude/settings.json. summarize-changes relays the admin's commands and no longer says a non-admin gets no workflow.

checks.text: The non-admin console sample in docs/cli.md matches the order run prints: the site note, the admin's steps, the workflow note from emit_files, then one line per file.
README.md:40 and docs/cli.md:222 (suggestion): two prose lines are left at 106 and 112 columns instead of the surrounding wrapping.
